options.label: the ambient layer only: the assistant above the product's screens, which stay exactly as they are
the full design architecture: the Foundation also governs tokens, spacing, radius and motion

decisions.why: A new project: nothing to preserve, so the whole system goes in.

options.label: express a reference (a screenshot, a link, a few words)

decisions.why: A new project: the look comes from whatever the person described in their request, else the Foundation's defaults.

css.where: in src/index.css: replace the existing `@import "tailwindcss";` with the first line, the other two right after it
css.why: theme(static) keeps every Tailwind variable emitted so the Foundation bridge can route through them.

adapt.why: vite is not a React Server Components app, so the layer's "use client" directives only print a bundler warning per file

envFlag.name: VITE_AMBIENT_STUBS
envFlag.default: stubs on unless the flag is "false"

transport.guidance: No API layer found: use the default src/lib/ambient/api.ts from start.md (stubs by default).

naming.note: vendored files keep kebab-case; tell the owner

warnings: The full path keeps all five icon libraries (the Foundation switches between them live; Remix is the heaviest); if bundle size matters, lazy-load Assistant (see mount.snippet shape).
The Foundation replaces the palette: host tests or visual baselines that assert the old colours will need updating.
The product depends on the `cn` npm package; the layer's `cn` comes from @/lib/utils (clsx + tailwind-merge). Do not swap one for the other.
